fixes.explanation: Donkey, friend! No chariot, no fancy ride, just a donkey and a plan. Mephibosheth says, “I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.” He says it right after he tells David he is lame (2 Samuel 19:26). Saddle up, ride along. I've had less clear plans than that, and I made mine in a junk drawer.

Ohhh, careful, friend, this one's a trap, and the trap is that it's true! Barzillai says it himself: “Your servant will go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan…” (2 Samuel 19:36). He's eighty years old and he knows his limits. He'll walk you to the river and a little past it, and then he's heading home.

A third? Friend, where did that number come from? Not from the text! It says, “All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king” (2 Samuel 19:40). Judah is ALL of them, Israel is HALF, and a third never shows up. Good thing the dough doesn't let me round off my measurements either.
